title: Deontic modal classification (scoped to the well-defined half of this todo; Flint role extraction remains a separate, unscoped follow-up)
goal: Classify a sentence's own modal (shall/must/may/can/should/will) into an explicit deontic operator (obligation/permission/prohibition), checked structurally against negation -- the part of EXP-087's original goal that is well-defined and buildable now, per that todo's own conclusion that the full Flint Actor/Activation-Condition/Act/Object role extraction 'likely needs its own narrower sub-exploration' and has no confirmed openly-released pretrained model.
method: lab.common.deontic.classify_deontic (new): finds a modal token (dep_=='aux', lemma in a small 6-word table) and checks its governing verb's own children for a 'neg' dependency -- the exact structural pattern spaCy uses for 'shall not'/'may not' (verified empirically before writing the classifier: 'not' attaches to the main verb, never to the modal token itself). Six hand-built cases covering every operator and both negation collapses, plus every sentence of the real GDPR_TEXT fixture (EXP-081), reporting every detected modal and operator honestly.
results_prose: 6/6 hand-built cases correct -- all correct. Both negation collapses verified: 'shall not' (negated obligation) and 'may not' (negated permission) both correctly classify as prohibition, not two different things. On the real 103-sentence GDPR text: 57 sentences contain a recognized modal, classified as {'permission': 7, 'obligation': 44, 'prohibition': 6}.
conclusion: Deontic classification alone -- the well-defined half of this todo, per its own stated uncertainty about the Flint role-extraction half -- works cleanly on both hand-built cases and the real GDPR text: 'shall'/'must' obligations, 'may'/'can' permissions, and both negated forms collapsing correctly to prohibition, all checked structurally against spaCy's own negation attachment, not a literal keyword scan. The full Flint Actor/Act/Object role extraction this todo also named remains genuinely unscoped and is not attempted here, consistent with the todo's own conclusion that it 'likely needs its own narrower sub-exploration' first.
scale_down: 'should' is mapped to the same 'obligation' bucket as 'shall'/'must' even though it is genuinely weaker (advisory, not strict) -- a real simplification, not a distinction this module makes. DEONTIC_TABLE covers 6 modals, not every English modal auxiliary (e.g. 'ought to', 'is required to' as a periphrastic alternative to 'must' are not recognized at all -- correctly returns operator=None, not guessed). The full Flint Actor/Activation-Condition/Act/Object role framework is NOT attempted -- this module says nothing about who the actor is or what act is governed, only the modal's own polarity.
follow_ups: The full Flint-style role extraction (Actor/Activation-Condition/Act/Object) remains unscoped -- determine first whether a fine-tuned role model/dataset is actually downloadable, or whether it must be built heuristically from dependency labels, before attempting it, per this todo's own original conclusion.

Wire classify_deontic's output into lab.common.inference so a rule's own modal strength (obligation vs permission) can eventually affect how its consequence is treated, which nothing in lab.common.inference does today.
models_used: spaCy en_core_web_sm dependency parser (lab.common.rules._parser, already a dependency, deterministic). No generative model, no new dependency.
